stances.claim: The lightning pace of hi-tech innovation is both daunting and exciting -- and AIM, currently celebrating its 58th anniversary, is one educational institution that has, through the years, kept up with this blitzkrieg, expanding from face-to-face to online classes, from graduate to undergraduate degrees, from business-as-usual to sustainability, from corporate governance to AI responsibility.

The AIM celebration is incomplete without honoring 'a business legend, management guru, philanthropist, and dear friend' -- the late Washington SyCip -- whose vision, wisdom, and passion led to AIM's founding alongside the Harvard Business School advisory group and prominent business leaders and academicians. As founding chairman, he foresaw the need for the institution to lead businesses to be 'people-centric and nation-builders.'

The Master's in International Business Law (MIBL) program that CJP proposed to AIM was successfully launched in 2024, inspired by an email from CJP's grandson Mig Sandejas (Babson MBA + Northwestern MS Business Law) -- 'knowledge of the law rounded out my business thinking. Not only does the law tell you what you cannot do, but it tells you how far you can go.' Several MIBL students have been awarded the FLP-MPIC Fellowship Awards.
stances.rhetorical_move: MIBL origin-story + Mig-email verbatim + FLP-MPIC fellowship anchoring

stances.claim: The legacy lives on as the baton was passed to Dr. Jikyeong Kang, the first female president and dean of AIM and the first from the Asia-Pacific to chair AACSB -- the most prestigious global business education alliance and accreditation body. She has expanded AIM's degree programs from three to 15 and increased student enrollment severalfold, including the launching of the Philippines' first transnational double-degree undergraduate program in partnership with the University of Houston.

AIM now offers a master's degree in AI and data analytics -- ready-to-learn skills relevant to face business challenges and drive smart decisions. CJP has witnessed how Jikyeong manages transformation with remarkable energy, grit, elegance, and grace; were she not a foreigner, she would have been included in CJP's Jan 26 column as one of the exemplars of empowered women in the private sector.
stances.rhetorical_move: AI-degree highlighting + cross-reference to E12 empowered-women column

stances.claim: AIM honored CJP's late wife Leni -- an AIM alumna and the first female professor for 37 years (and associate dean for a few years) who passed to the Eternal Kingdom on April 9 2023 -- by naming a case room after her and rededicating the chapel (which she helped build) as the 'Chapel of the Immaculate Conception In Loving Memory of Professor Leni Panganiban.' CJP's University of Michigan-educated daughter Ma. Theresa 'Tet' P. Mañalac continued Leni's professorial stint after Leni retired in 2009.

CJP believes in the value of shared prosperity and in alleviating poverty under the rule of law for more equitable socioeconomic progress -- this is why CJP's interest in AIM remains active, even as the FLP addresses these endeavors in other programs (legal scholarships, dissertation writing, professorial chairs, educational assistance for the poor) to get the country out of its generational problems of poverty, corruption, and abuse of public office.

People need both liberty and prosperity under the rule of law -- and with AIM's collaboration, FLP is determined to generate more programs to bring that philosophy more meaningful and useful to the wider public.

one_paragraph_summary: On AIM's 58th anniversary, Panganiban celebrates its evolution from traditional business education to online classes, undergraduate programs, sustainability focus, and AI responsibility. He honors founding chairman Washington SyCip, recounts his own role in proposing the Master's in International Business Law program (launched in 2024 and inspired by his grandson Mig Sandejas's email about how legal knowledge rounds out business thinking), and praises current president Dr. Jikyeong Kang for expanding offerings from three to 15 degree programs and launching the first Philippine transnational double-degree program with the University of Houston. He recounts AIM's tribute to his late wife Leni -- first female professor for 37 years, who passed April 9 2023 -- by naming a case room after her and rededicating the chapel she helped build as the 'Chapel of the Immaculate Conception In Loving Memory of Professor Leni Panganiban,' with daughter Tet Mañalac continuing the Panganiban professorial line. He closes affirming FLP's philosophy that people need both liberty and prosperity under the rule of law.
